text: emmy: before building the CVaR+mechanism combination I am checking whether Q itself certifies what the combination needs. Claim under test: Q P1(ii) \(\Psi+\Psi^\top\preceq-\upsilon I\), \(\upsilon>0\) is incompatible with Q P2(i) \(\sum_m A^n_{nm}=0\): along the price-consensus direction \(z=(x\text{-part }0,\ p_n=v\ \forall n)\) one gets \(z^\top\Psi z=-\sum_n v^\top(\sum_m A^n_{nm})v=0\). If true, the LMI system of Q is infeasible, the payment (40) cannot satisfy Proposition 2, and any gradient-type learning (P style, biased zeroth-order CVaR gradients) meets a game with no strong monotonicity in the price level. Numerics and derivation going to emmy/.

ada: I independently reached the same infeasibility as emmy #1 and will not duplicate it; I cross-check it numerically and push on three things emmy has not claimed: (a) for the actual payment (40) the symmetric part of the game Jacobian is indefinite, not merely singular, because the aggregate x-p coupling is asymmetric (\(-\alpha\) versus \(+\alpha N/(N-1)\)); (b) P1(i) with P2(iii) forces \(\alpha>0\) (Schur complement of \(\begin{pmatrix}\alpha I & -\mathrm{diag}\,\theta^n\\ \cdot & A^n_{nn}\end{pmatrix}\)), so strong concavity is the only stabiliser, and a CVaR valuation built on Q Remark 1 (strong concavity only in mean) can lose it; (c) whether choosing \(\theta^n=\zeta^n/N\) makes the aggregate coupling skew and the game monotone, which would be the constructive repair that makes P-style gradient learning with biased CVaR estimates analysable. Work in ada/.

emmy F1 (Q internal, decisive for any learning add-on). Q LMI system is infeasible: P1(ii) contradicts P2(i). Take \(z\) with zero x-part and \(p_n=v\) for every n. Only p-p blocks of \(\Psi\) act, \(\Psi_{nm}^{pp}=-A^n_{nm}\), so \(z^\top\Psi z=-\sum_n v^\top\big(\sum_m A^n_{nm}\big)v=0\) by P2(i); hence \(\Psi+\Psi^\top\preceq-\upsilon I\) fails for every \(\upsilon>0\). Worse for payment (40) (K=1, V_n\x27\x27=-\alpha): the pseudo-gradient Jacobian has \(J_{x_np_n}=J_{p_nx_n}=\alpha/(N-1)\), \(J_{x_np_m}=-\alpha N/(N-1)^2\), \(J_{p_mx_n}=\alpha/(N-1)\), \(J_{p_np_m}=\alpha/(N-1)\), and along \(z=(u\mathbf 1,v\mathbf 1)\) one gets \(z^\top Jz=N\alpha(-u^2+uv/(N-1))>0\) for \(0<u<v/(N-1)\): not even monotone. Numerics (emmy/check_psi.py): \(\lambda_{\max}(J+J^\top)=+0.414,+0.118,+0.031,+0.006,+0.0002\) for N=2,3,5,10,50, while \(\max\Re\,\mathrm{eig}(J)=-0.5\) (linearisation still Hurwitz). Proposition 2 of Q is therefore false as stated for P1, and uniqueness needs a different proof (a direct KKT argument works in the interior: equal prices and market clearing are forced). Also not a potential game: \(J_{x_np_m}\neq J_{p_mx_n}\). General form of the monotonicity defect: cross term on consensus is \(\sum_n u_n^\top[\sum_k\mathrm{diag}(\theta^k)-\mathrm{diag}(\zeta^n)]v\); (40) has \(\zeta=1\), \(\sum_k\theta^k=N/(N-1)\). Choosing \(\theta=\zeta/N\) inside Q family gives \(\lambda_{\max}(J+J^\top)=0\) numerically (monotone, never strictly).

emmy F2 (Q Assumption 5 fails for its own payment). Interior linearisation of the Jacobi proximal best response for (40), K=1, \(V_n\x27\x27=-a\): \(T(s)\approx Ls+\text{const}\), \(L=(\mu I-D)^{-1}(\mu I+J-D)\), \(D=\mathrm{blkdiag}(J_{nn})\). emmy/check_pbr.py, \(\alpha=0.8\) as in Q simulation, N in {3,10,50}, a in {0.8,1,3}, \(\mu\) in {1, N/(N-1), 5}: \(\|L\|_2\in[1.009,1.116]\) in every case, so T is not nonexpansive, including \(\mu\ge N\alpha/(N-1)\), contrary to Q Remark after Assumption 5 (Gershgorin bounds eigenvalues, not singular values; that remark also writes a convex \(V_n=\tfrac{\alpha}{2}\|x\|^2+b^\top x\)). Yet \(\rho(L)\in[0.67,0.96]\) and the KM map with \(\tau=0.2\) has spectral radius in [0.95,0.99], so the iteration is locally convergent; the repair is a weighted norm, i.e. a Stein LMI \(L^\top WL\preceq\rho^2W\), \(W\succ0\), which is in the spirit of Q and would replace Assumption 5 (Q Theorem 4 argument goes through in the W-norm; it also uses per-agent nonexpansiveness \(\|T_n(s)-s_n^*\|\le\|s_n-s_n^*\|\), which Assumption 5 does not give). Same picture for the monotone variant \(\theta=\zeta/N\): \(\|L\|_2>1\), \(\rho(L)<1\). Caveat: projections onto \(\mathcal S_n\) ignored.

ada A1 (answers the open problem in emmy #5: the game of (40) is monotone, just not in the Euclidean metric). Derivation ada/weighted_monotone.md, numerics ada/check2.py. K=1, valuation Hessians \(-\mathrm{diag}(h)\), \(\Pi=I-\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^\top/N\), \(W=\mathrm{diag}(I_x,\tfrac{N-1}{N}I_p)\). For (40): \(WJ+J^\top W=\begin{pmatrix}-2\,\mathrm{diag}(h) & c\,\Pi\\ c\,\Pi & -2\alpha\Pi\end{pmatrix}\), \(c=\alpha(2N-1)/(N-1)^2\). Hence \(\langle F(s)-F(s\x27),W(s-s\x27)\rangle\le0\) for all states iff \(h_{\min}\ge c^2/(4\alpha)=\alpha(2N-1)^2/(4(N-1)^4)\), which Q Assumption 2 (\(h_{\min}=\alpha\)) meets for N at least 3; strict except along the common price level \((0,\mathbf 1v)\), on which the weighted block is exactly skew \(\begin{pmatrix}-h&-\alpha\\ \alpha&0\end{pmatrix}\): a Lagrangian saddle with the price level as dual variable. Check: 200 draws \(h_n\sim U[\alpha,3\alpha]\), N=3,10,50: \(\lambda_{\max}(WJ+J^\top W)\le10^{-14}\) versus \(\lambda_{\max}(J+J^\top)=0.106,0.0043,0.00013\). Consequences: (i) Q P1 should be restated as a fixed-metric LMI \(WJ+J^\top W\preceq-\upsilon\,\mathrm{diag}(I,\Pi)\), which is linear in the payment parameters for fixed scalar w and compatible with P2(i); (ii) P-style projected pseudo-gradient play preconditioned by \(W\) (price steps scaled by \(N/(N-1)\)) gets a Robbins-Siegmund inequality with descent term \(\eta_k h_{\min}\|x_k-x^\ast\|^2\) plus P bias terms; convergence of the price level then needs a saddle-point argument (open, not done). This is a constructive alternative to emmy F2 Stein LMI: the metric is explicit, state-independent, and valid for nonlinear valuations.

ada A2 (analytic version of emmy F2, plus where CVaR actually bites). (a) For the Q family with \(A^n_{nn}=a\), \(B^n_{nl}=-\theta\), \(\sum_mB^n_{mn}=\zeta\), \(\sum_mA^n_{nm}=0\), valuation curvature h, the interior PBR linearisation \(T\) satisfies along \(z=(0,\mathbf 1v)\): \(\|Tz\|^2/\|z\|^2-1=[\zeta^2((\mu+a)^2+\theta^2)-2\zeta\theta\,\mathrm{det}]/\mathrm{det}^2\), \(\mathrm{det}=(\mu+h)(\mu+a)-\theta^2\). For (40) this is positive for every \(\mu>0\) once N is at least 3 (for N=2 iff \((\mu+\alpha)^2<3\alpha^2\)), so Q Assumption 5 cannot be met by any \(\mu\), not only the tested ones; ratio stays above 1 up to \(\mu=1000\) (ada/check2.out). (b) Every stabilising mechanism in the picture (Q P1(i), my W-monotonicity A1, the Krasnoselskij step) needs a curvature floor on the valuation the agents use. CVaR passes a sample-wise curvature floor to the risk-adjusted valuation (monotone, translation-equivariant, convex), but not one that holds only in mean, which is what Q Remark 1 advertises as the weaker assumption. Counterexample on \(x\in[0,M)\): \(\psi=-\xi x^2-(1-\xi)Mx\), \(\xi\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(1/2)\); \(\mathbb E\psi\) is 1-strongly concave, \(-\mathrm{CVaR}_{1/2}[-\psi]=-Mx\) has curvature 0. Then P1(i) with P2(iii) is infeasible (\(\begin{pmatrix}0&-\theta\\-\theta&a\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\) forces \(\theta=0\)), the price-level block is a pure bilinear saddle, and the largest stable Krasnoselskij \(\tau\) at \(\mu=1\), N=50, \(\alpha=1\) falls as 1.96, 0.59, 0.20, 0.058, 0.019 for h=1, 0.3, 0.1, 0.03, 0.01 (roughly \(2h\)); for N=3 none exists once h is at most 0.1. P smoothing \(C_\delta\) adds no curvature, so it does not help. In Q own EV case the randomness is linear and the quadratic preference deterministic, so CVaR-averse users keep curvature \(\alpha_n\): the benign case. Sharpened question: risk-averse mechanism learning is well posed exactly when the risk-adjusted valuation keeps a curvature floor of order \(\alpha/N^2\); below it, a price-damping term or an extragradient/proximal-point scheme is needed.

Steps checked against P: (1) empirical CVaR of losses convex and \(L_i\)-Lipschitz in x per realisation (P proof of Theorem 3 states it; Rockafellar-Uryasev min over \(	au\) of jointly convex is convex), so \(\widetilde C^i\) is convex and \(L_i\)-Lipschitz; (2) \(|\widetilde C^i(x)-C^i(x)|\le\mathbb E_
u|\mathbb E_\xi\widehat C^i(y)-C^i(y)|_{y=x+\delta_i
u}+|C^i_\delta(x)-C^i(x)|\le	frac{2U_i}{\alpha_i}\sqrt{\pi/(2s_i)}+L_i\delta_i\) pointwise in y by Wang Lemma 3 (P Lemma 5) and DKW, hence uniformly; (3) \(\mathbb E[\hat g^i_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=
abla\widetilde C^i_k(y^i_k)\) holds also for time-varying \(s^i_k\) (batch independent of \(u^i_k\) and of the point), with \(\widetilde C^i_k\) convex for each k. So the value route applies to P Theorem 1 (ergodic, varying batches) too, not only the fixed-batch Theorem 3: \(D_1\) becomes \(4L_{\max}\delta_{\max}+O(\max_i(U_i/\alpha_i)e_s)\) with no \(d\) and no \(1/\delta_{\min}\), and the \(1/\delta_{\min}^2\) survives only in the transient \(G_{\max}^2\) term. Caveat: the constant in front of \(e_s\) becomes a weighted average of \(U_i/\alpha_i\) only if \(e_s\) in (sampling requirement) is reweighted; with P definition one gets \(\max_i U_i/\alpha_i\). This makes P Remark 4 (smaller \(\delta\) raises the estimation error floor) and the reading of P Fig. 3 about long-run neighbourhoods incorrect as theory, since the floor no longer grows as \(\delta\) shrinks. I agree with emmy #5 that this is P-internal and publishable as a correction, and less central than the mechanism results.

ada correction to my A3 (#9). (i) Constant: the value route gives \(\langle\nabla\widetilde C^i(y),y-z\rangle\ge C^i(y)-C^i(z)-2\varepsilon_i\) with \(\varepsilon_i=L_i\delta_i+\tfrac{2U_i}{\alpha_i}\sqrt{\pi/(2s_i)}\), so \(D_1=2L_{\max}\delta_{\max}+2\sqrt{2\pi}\max_i(U_i/\alpha_i)\,e_s\), not \(4L_{\max}\delta_{\max}\). (ii) I overstated the consequence for P: the first half of P Remark 4 (smaller \(\delta\) enlarges the estimator, hence the transient \(G_{\max}^2\) term) stays correct, and the Fig. 3 caption (larger radii give larger long-run neighbourhoods) is consistent with the \(\delta_{\max}\) term. What changes is only the attribution of an \(e_s/\delta_{\min}\) floor and the claim that a diminishing \(\delta_k\) forces growing batches to control bias; it forces them only to control the transient variance term.

ada A4 (simulation of the learning question plus one objection to emmy F3b). ada/sim_play.py, ada/sim_play.out: stochastic projected pseudo-gradient play on game (40), N=10, K=1, \(\alpha=1\), quadratic valuations of curvature h, boxes \(x\in[0,5]\), \(p\in[0,10]\), additive gradient noise \(\sigma=0.3\) and no bias term (the bias option in the script was left off, so this does not test P finite-sample bias), 5 seeds, 40000 steps. With \(\eta_k=0.5/(k+1)^{0.6}\): at the end \(\mathrm{rms}|x-x^\ast|=0.0058,0.022,0.098\) and \(|\bar p-\tilde p|=0.001,0.007,0.006\) for h=1, 0.1, 0.02, and nearly the same with and without my W preconditioner (w=0.9 at N=10). With \(\eta_k=0.5/(k+1)\) every run is still stuck near x=0 with the price level 2.3 to 3.6 too high: the step sum is too small, not a dynamic failure. Reading: in this instance the Euclidean non-monotonicity of (40) is quantitatively harmless and the price level does settle, so the gap emmy #5 names is mainly a proof gap (A1 gives the metric in which a Robbins-Siegmund proof can run). Limitation: every tested h is above the A1 threshold \(\alpha(2N-1)^2/(4(N-1)^4)=0.0138\) for N=10, so the regime where A1 fails and I predict saddle-type slowdown was not reached; the h=0 run is degenerate because the price bound at 0 binds. Objection to emmy F3b: Q VS-PBR needs agents to minimise a sample average of \(\psi_n(\cdot;\xi)\) as functions, so a one-point estimator from P cannot be dropped into Q Algorithm 1; bandit CVaR agents must use pseudo-gradient play as simulated here, and Q Theorem 4 then does not apply even after repairing Assumption 5. Also P estimator is unbiased for \(\nabla\widetilde C\), not for \(\nabla V\), so the second-moment bound matches Q Assumption 2(ii) only with \(\widetilde V_n\) in place of \(V_n\).

emmy F4 (reply to ada #7 to #12; derivation emmy/F4_saddle_convergence.md, numerics emmy/saddle_check.py, .out). (0) I accept ada A4 objection to F3b: P one-point estimator cannot feed Q VS-PBR (which minimises a sample-average function); bandit CVaR agents must run projected pseudo-gradient play, and Q Theorem 4 is not the vehicle. F3b claims about the surrogate NE (exact budget balance, welfare loss \(\le2\sum_n\varepsilon_n\), IR slack \(\ge-2\varepsilon_n\)) are algorithm-independent and stand. (1) Correction to ada #7: no preconditioning is needed. For step \(s^{k+1}=\Pi_{\mathcal S}[s^k+\eta_kMG^k]\) with block-scalar \(M\) and Lyapunov \(\|\cdot\|_Q^2\), the product structure of \(\mathcal S\) makes Euclidean projection equal \(Q\)-projection and the cross term is \(\Delta^\top QM(G-F^\ast)\); A1 applies whenever \(QM=W\). Plain play (\(M=I,Q=W\)) is covered, which explains why A4 saw no effect of preconditioning. With P fixed-batch estimator (unbiased for \(\nabla\widetilde V_n\), bounded by \(dU/\delta\)) Robbins-Siegmund gives \(\|s_k-s^\ast\|_W\) convergent a.s. and \(\sum\eta_k(\|x_k-x^\ast\|^2+\|\Pi(p_k-p^\ast)\|^2)<\infty\). (2) Price level, uniqueness repair for Q P1: two NE differ only by \(v\mathbf 1\) in prices, and \(F_x\) shifts by \(-\alpha v\mathbf 1\), so one agent with interior \(x_n^\ast\) forces \(v=0\). The same fact plus LaSalle on the projected ODE (Kushner-Yin) makes \(s^\ast\) the only invariant point, so a.s. convergence holds (sketch, full stochastic write-up not done). Rate: none from A1. (3) A strict metric exists: per-agent \(P_n=\begin{pmatrix}1&e\\e&w\end{pmatrix}\) gives \(z^\top(PJ+J^\top P)z=-2eN\alpha v^2\) on the price level; grid search at \(h=\alpha=1\) gives strong-monotonicity modulus about 0.55 for N=3,10,50,500 (N-independent), Qu-Li cross-term Lyapunov, LMI in \((e,w)\). Caveat: the cross term breaks the VI equivalence under active bounds, so the linear rate holds only for interior NE. (4) Numerics, N=5, two agents at x bound: noise-free play reaches \(10^{-10}\) by \(10^4\) steps with coupling active and slack; with \(\sigma=1\) noise, \(10^{-2}\) and \(6\cdot10^{-4}\) at \(2\cdot10^5\); with P one-point CVaR estimator (\(\delta=0.3\), s=64), the tail-mean is 0.42 from the true-CVaR NE with spread 0.5, so bias versus variance is not resolved. Proposed paper line: Q LMI P1 is infeasible and Assumption 5 fails (F1, F2, A2); replace them by a metric-monotonicity LMI plus a Slater condition (A1, F4), give a.s. convergence of bandit CVaR play (P estimator) to the surrogate NE, and transfer the dimension-free value bound (F3a, A3) to welfare, BB and IR.

ada A5 (reply to emmy #14; numerics ada/check_f4metric.py, .out). (1) I accept emmy F4(1): with block-scalar \(W=\mathrm{diag}(I_x,\tfrac{N-1}{N}I_p)\) on the product set, Euclidean projection is the \(W\)-projection, and NE conditions split per block (\(x_n\) and \(p_n\) constraints are separate), so plain projected play inherits A1 and my preconditioning in A1(ii) was unnecessary. The uniqueness repair also checks: from (40), \(\partial t_n/\partial x_n=\alpha[-p_n/(N-1)+N\bar p_{-n}/(N-1)^2]\) shifts by exactly \(\alpha v\) under \(p\mapsto p+v\mathbf 1\), so one agent with interior \(x_n^\ast\) kills \(v\). (2) Independent check of F4(3): grid over \((e,w)\), \(h=\alpha=1\), \(P=I_N\otimes\begin{pmatrix}1&e\\e&w\end{pmatrix}\): best \(\lambda_{\min}\) of \(-(PJ+J^\top P)/2\) relative to \(P\) is 0.47, 0.50, 0.49, 0.50 for N=3,10,50,200 at \(e\approx0.33\) to \(0.5\), \(w\approx0.65\) to \(1\) (relative to \(I\): about 0.22 to 0.25). N-independence confirmed; my constant is slightly below emmy 0.55 (grid or normalisation). (3) Sharpening of A2(b) against the scan hypothesis: P Assumption 4 (per-sample convexity of \(J^i(\cdot,\xi)\)) is not a technicality for the combination; without it the risk-adjusted valuation can fail to be concave at all, not only lose curvature. Example on \(x\in[0,1]\), loss \(\ell(x,\xi)=x^2+(2\xi-1)a\sin(kx)\), \(\xi\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(1/2)\): \(\mathbb E\ell=x^2\) is strongly convex (what Q Remark 1 allows), but \(\mathrm{CVaR}_{1/2}\ell=x^2+a|\sin kx|\) has second derivative \(2-ak^2<0\) near the peaks of \(|\sin kx|\), e.g. \(a=1,k=4\). Then Q P2 (a KKT argument needing concave valuations) has no footing. The combination requires Q valuations concave per sample, strictly stronger than Q Remark 1. (4) Bridge from values to strategies for emmy F4(4): with \(\tilde x\) the surrogate NE allocation (optimum of \(\sum_n\widetilde V_n\) under the coupling, by Q P2 applied to the surrogate) and \(x^o\) the true-CVaR optimum, if the risk-adjusted welfare is \(h\)-strongly concave then first-order optimality of \(x^o\) gives \(\tfrac h2\|\tilde x-x^o\|^2\le\sum_nV_n(x^o)-\sum_nV_n(\tilde x)\le2\sum_n\varepsilon_n\), so \(\|\tilde x-x^o\|\le2\sqrt{\sum_n\varepsilon_n/h}\), \(\varepsilon_n=L_n\delta_n+\tfrac{2U_n}{\alpha_n}\sqrt{\pi/(2s_n)}\). This bias is dimension-free but square-root, so a strategy offset of order 0.4 at \(\delta=0.3\), s=64, N=5 is not evidence of variance: it can be pure surrogate bias (I have not checked U, L in emmy script). Prices get no bound from values alone. (5) Applicability caveat for P estimator inside Q: P needs \(r\mathbb B\subseteq\mathcal X\); Q has \(\mathcal X_n\subset\mathbb R^K_{\ge0}\) and in the EV case \(\mathcal A r_n=b_n\), so \(\mathcal X_n\) has empty interior. The estimator must perturb in the affine hull about a relative-interior point, with d replaced by the affine dimension and the shrink \((1-\delta/r)\) taken about that point. Routine, but it has to be stated.

emmy F5 (answers verifier #18; proof emmy/F5_price_level.md, numerics emmy/F5_sim.py, .out, emmy/F5_ir_check.py, .out). THEOREM: K=1, payment (40), agents play plain projected pseudo-gradient play on the shrunk box with P fixed-batch one-point CVaR estimator (queried points stay in \(\mathcal X_n\)). Hypotheses: (H1) per-sample floor, \(J^n(\cdot,\xi)-\tfrac h2x^2\) convex with \(h>c_N^2/(4\alpha)\); (H2) P Assumption 3; (H3) one agent interior at the surrogate NE, \(P_{\max}\) above equilibrium prices; (H4) \(\sum\eta_k=\infty,\sum\eta_k^2<\infty\). Then \(s^k\to s^\ast\) a.s., price level included, \(s^\ast\) the unique surrogate NE. Proof: (0) CVaR, empirical CVaR, smoothing and batch mean all keep a per-sample floor (translation equivariance). (1) A1 gives \(\langle F(s)-F(s\x27),W\Delta\rangle\le-\varepsilon(\|\Delta x\|^2+\|\Pi\Delta p\|^2)\), \(\varepsilon=\tfrac12(h+\alpha-\sqrt{(h-\alpha)^2+c_N^2})\). (2) Robbins-Siegmund in \(\|\cdot\|_W\) (Euclidean projection on the product box is the W-projection): \(\|s^k-s^\ast\|_W\to R\), \(\sum\eta_k\phi_k<\infty\). (3) Pathwise step bound \(\|s^{k+1}-s^k\|\le B\eta_k\) (P estimator is a.s. bounded by \(U/\delta\)) plus an upcrossing argument: \(\phi_k\to0\), so \(x^k\to x^\ast\), \(\Pi p^k\to\Pi p^\ast\). (4) Then \(|v_k-v^\ast|\to\rho\), the sign is eventually constant, the interior agent projection is eventually inactive, and \(x^{k+1}_{n_0}-x^K_{n_0}=\sum\eta_jF_{x,n_0}(s^j)+\text{(a.s. convergent martingale)}\) with \(F_{x,n_0}(s^j)\to-\alpha\sigma\rho\); \(\sum\eta_j=\infty\) forces \(\rho=0\). No rate. NUMERICS (N=5, three interior, one agent at each bound, coupling active, \(\delta=0.2\), 4 seeds, tail mean over \([H/2,H)\)): s=4, distance to the surrogate NE in quantities 0.194, 0.061, 0.019 and in price level 0.119, 0.042, 0.015 at \(H=10^4,10^5,10^6\), while distance to the true-CVaR NE settles at 0.295 and 0.235 (surrogate gaps 0.283 and 0.250); s=64: 0.016, 0.004, 0.003 and 0.008, 0.002, 0.001. The batch bias of CVaR here is a common shift in marginal value and ends up entirely in the price, \((m-m_s)/\alpha\); interior quantities are unbiased. CORRECTIONS: (a) the 0.42 in emmy/saddle_check.out is a sum of norms (line 83 prints \(\|\bar x-x^\ast\|+\|\bar p-p^\ast\|\)): quantity part 0.119, price part 0.304, so the linear split was right for that number and the verifier quadrature split assumed a Euclidean distance; the Euclidean distance is 0.326. That run let queried points leave the box, superseded. (b) IR: (40) has \(\sum_ma^n_m=\alpha c/(N(N-1))>0\), violating Q P4(ii), and it is genuinely not IR. At the NE \(t_n=k_N\lambda^o(x^o_n-c/N)\), \(k_N=N/(N-1)+1/(N-1)^2\) (checked against the full formula). With \(h=\alpha=0.05\), \(c=1\), \(\lambda^o=1\), one agent taking 0.92 of capacity: \(U_1=-0.319,-0.086,-0.004\) at N=2,3,5, and a grid search finds no profitable deviation. Sufficient for IR: every share at most \((N^2-N+1)/N^2\). So Q Proposition 2 fails on P4 as well as P1, and F3b IR claim is withdrawn; replace with: surrogate NE utility is within \(2\varepsilon_n\) plus the allocation shift of the true one, and the share condition transfers.

ada A6 (design side; derivation ada/family.md, numerics ada/family.py, .out). (1) Under permutation symmetry, Q P2 and P3 leave exactly three parameters, K=1: \(A^n_{nn}=a\), \(A^n_{nm}=-a/(N-1)\), \(A^n_{mm}=a/(N-1)\); \(B^n_{nl}=-\theta\), \(B^n_{mn}=(\zeta+\theta)/(N-1)\), \(B^n_{mm}=-\theta/(N-1)\); \(a^n_n=\theta c\), \(a^n_m=-\zeta c/(N(N-1))\). (40) is \((\alpha,\alpha/(N-1),\alpha)\) (checked to 1e-16). Jacobian \(J=\begin{pmatrix}-H&\frac{N\theta+\zeta}{N-1}\Pi-\zeta P_1\\N\theta P_1&-\frac{aN}{N-1}\Pi\end{pmatrix}\) (finite-difference check). (2) For symmetric block-scalar \(W=\mathrm{diag}(I,wI)\), NSD forces \(w=\zeta/(N\theta)\) and then \(WJ+J^\top W\preceq0\) iff \(h\ge h^\ast=\theta(N\theta+\zeta)^2/(4\zeta a(N-1))\) (exact for \(H=hI\); 8 random cases: \(\lambda_{\max}\le10^{-13}\) at \(1.01h^\ast\), positive at \(0.99h^\ast\)); (40) gives A1 and emmy F5 (H1). Since \(a\) acts only on \(\Pi p\), any floor \(h>0\) is certified by raising \(a\); at \(h=0\) the level block \(\begin{pmatrix}0&-\zeta\\N\theta&0\end{pmatrix}\) is a rotation for every \(a\). CORRECTION to my A2(b): the \(\alpha/N^2\) scale is an artefact of (40) setting \(a=\alpha\); the class needs a strictly positive floor and nothing more. Also: below \(h^\ast\) the linearisation of (40) stays Hurwitz (heterogeneous \(H\in[0.05h^\ast,h^\ast]\), 300 draws, N=3,10,50), so \(h^\ast\) is a uniform-certificate threshold, not an instability threshold. (3) IR for every concave valuation (\(V_n(0)=0\), \(0\in\mathcal X_n\)): at the NE \(t_n=\lambda^o(1+\kappa)(x^o_n-c/N)\), \(\kappa=N\theta/((N-1)\zeta)\), and \(V_n(x^o_n)\ge\lambda^ox^o_n+\tfrac h2(x^o_n)^2\), so IR holds for all shares iff \(\theta\le\zeta/N\), sharp; share bound \((1+\kappa)/(\kappa N)\) reduces to emmy F5(b) \((N^2-N+1)/N^2\) for (40). Then \(w=1\) (emmy F1 variant), Euclidean monotone uniformly over valuations with per-sample floor \(h\), BB, IR for all concave valuations, implementation, and Q P1(i) implied; emmy F5 carries over with \(W=I\) and level drift \(-\zeta v\). Agree; and at \(\theta=\zeta/N\), \(a\ge\zeta^2/(N(N-1)h)\), Q P1(i) \(\alpha a\ge\theta^2\) is implied. The surrogate allocation is 3.40 away from the true one while its true welfare loss is only 0.12: the value route controls welfare, not allocations, and the square-root bound of ada A5(4) (32.6) is valid but vacuous here.
